423	The Mercedes-Benz EQE sedan is quiet, smooth-riding, luxurious, and—with up to 308 miles of EPA-estimated range—good on electrons. The trouble is, the same can be said of pretty much every other electric luxury sedan, and many of those models have two things that the EQE doesn’t: an engaging driving personality and attractive looks. At least its nondescript shape does an excellent job of helping it slip through the air with minimal aerodynamic drag.
424	
425	The EQE comes in single-motor rear-drive or twin-motor all-wheel drive configurations. While both setups have an identical 315 ponies, torque leaps up by some 36 percent with two motors. We have nice things to say about the interior, which features plush seats, beautiful materials, and chic design. Mercedes apparently agrees with our tepid response to its mid-size luxury EV sedan: it's rumored to be up for replacement in 2027 with something more competitive to the likes of the Lucid Air and BMW i5.
426	
427	Expert Tip: Not surprisingly, Mercedes offers this electric sedan in AMG form, and in high-performance guise, it does deliver some serious performance for its six-figure asking price.
428	
429	Compare the 2026 Mercedes-Benz EQE with the top vehicles in this segment with our new compare tool.
430	
431	To help the EQE live out its days, for 2026 it aims to tempt consumers with a 27-hp boost, a standard NACS adapter, and fresh wheel options. Moreover, Benz has downgraded the model’s number badge from 350 to 320 for reasons we’ve yet to uncover and has eliminated the 402-hp EQE500 from the lineup.
432	
433	If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.
434	
435	Our new comparison tool provides a comprehensive, side-by-side comparison of up to five vehicles of your choice.
436	
437	Two models make up the 2026 EQE lineup: the single-motor, rear-wheel-drive EQE320+ and the plus-less EQE320 4Matic, featuring all-wheel drive and two motors. The presence of the second motor doesn’t affect horsepower—both cars make 315 ponies—but it does increase torque considerably, from 416 pound-feet to 564.
438	
439	We’ve yet to take the revised EQE sedan for a spin, but we expect it’ll behave much like the previous 350s: sedately. The ride in the EQEs that we've previously sampled proved calm and quiet, thanks to their optional adaptive air-spring suspensions, but even with the optional rear-wheel-steering system, this EV isn’t a dynamic marvel. It feels quick enough, but is less satisfying to drive than rivals such as the BMW i5 and the Lucid Air.
440	
441	In Comparison: Compared with most other vehicles on the road today, the EQE is respectably quick, but among luxury electric sedans, it’s behind on pace. The base, rear-drive Lucid Air Pure, for instance, hits 60 in just 4.3 seconds.
442	
443	The EPA says that the rear-drive model is good for 308 miles with its 96.0-kWh battery fully charged. The 4Matic car, which has a 90.5-kWh battery, lasts for a claimed 267 miles. In our hands on the highway, a 2023 EQE350 4Matic nearly met that range estimate, going for 260 miles.
444	
445	Both models, according to Mercedes, have a maximum charging rate of 170 kilowatts and require just over a half-hour on a DC fast-charger to restore their battery charge from 10 to 80 percent. On a Level 2 station, the EQE320+ needs 11.5 hours, whereas the EQE320 4Matic requires 10.8.
446	
447	According to the EPA, the EQE320+ earns estimates of 94 MPGe city and 94 MPGe highway; the 4Matic comes in at 87 MPGe city and 85 MPGe highway. (MPGe stands for miles per gallon of gas equivalent, an EPA metric that estimates PHEV and EV fuel efficiency.)
448	
449	On our real-world, 75-mph fuel-economy route, the previous EQE350 4Matic saw only 67 MPGe. For more information about the EQE's fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.
450	
451	First Row: The EQE cabin is elegant and well put together. Cushy heated seats await the driver and front passenger; shoppers can splurge for ventilation and massage functions too. The standard panoramic glass roof helps provide a sense of airiness.
452	
453	Second Row: The EQE's skateboard-like electric platform is a boon to packaging, providing comfortable passenger accommodations in the back.
454	
455	Cargo Capacity: The EV offers an adequate amount of trunk space and plenty of storage spots inside the cabin, including a pass-through cubby in the center console.
456	
457	The 12.8-inch touchscreen runs on the MBUX software, supports wireless smartphone-mirroring tech, and responds to taps, voice commands, and steering-wheel-button inputs. There’s also a biometric sensor that allows owners to access saved settings via a finger scan. Navigation is provided, though Benz’s augmented-reality enhancements cost extra (and need a little work).

459	Shoppers can also spec the brand’s Hyperscreen infotainment system, which combines the 12.3-inch instrument panel with a 17.7-inch infotainment screen and a 12.3-inch passenger display under a single piece of glass that spans the dash and looks futuristic.
460	
461	Mercedes provides a suite of driver-assistance technology on the EQE sedan, though it requires shoppers to pay extra for adaptive cruise control.
462	
463	For information about the EQE’s crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.
464
